summary: An excerpt from a novel (Book 10, part 83) following a woman who leads the Association for a Human-Readable World and her ongoing rivalry with Damian, whose family keeps in touch with her through handwritten notes. Her staff struggle as their network devices repeatedly fail, the embedded journalists leave, and the city falls into winter gloom. The passage ends with a second nationwide "Downtime" that halts the country for eight days on Valentine's Day.
one_line: In a fictional winter, network failures and a second nationwide Downtime disrupt the Association for a Human-Readable World and its rivalry with Damian.
key_facts: Damian's great-aunt sent a note with best wishes from Damian's mother, which the protagonist read while boiling the kettle.
The great-aunt wanted to know if the protagonist had met a nice boy in DC yet, but did not say so directly.
The protagonist and the old lady kept writing to each other partly so the Relatives could be reassured that someone capable was watching out for Damian's interests.
The protagonist and Damian had half a dozen more skirmishes that month, with her phone reactivating whenever she came within shouting distance of him.
The on-again/off-again hearings in Judiciary and Commerce never quite materialized.
Stuart was an engineer living in Borujerd, who was a fast learner with much deeper pockets and working network infrastructure.
The protagonist's Board approved renting an empty suite of offices below their office to convert into bedrooms for staff on days when their cars could not get them home.
Staff secretly borrowed elderly network appliances from relatives or bought them at the Salvation Army dollar-a-pound bin.
Within a few hours of being in the possession of Association staff, the devices seized up and lost their network routes.
The embedded journalists went home after the second week, as their own equipment was also failing.
The paralegal quit because she needed a job where the phones worked so she could call her girlfriend.
The press stopped calling after the media guy took a series of "personal days."
February arrived with ice, slush, and perpetual twilight in the city.
The second Downtime struck during morning rush-hour on Valentine's Day, a Monday.
The second Downtime halted the whole country for eight long days.
During the Downtime hospitals overflowed and doctors used motorized scooters to travel between places.
